title: Uranus Is at Its Best Tonight
summary:
One of the hardest planets to see is putting on its best show of the year. On Wednesday, November 25, the faraway ice planet Uranus reaches its yearly opposition. That is when it is closest to Earth this year, and it looks at its brightest.

Opposition happens when Earth moves between Uranus and the sun. The moment of opposition is at 6 p.m. ET on November 25. Uranus will rise in the east around sunset, reach its highest point around midnight, and set in the west around sunrise.

You can find it in the group of stars called Taurus, close to the Pleiades star cluster, also known as the Seven Sisters. Uranus will be a little way to the southeast of the cluster.

Uranus is very faint. Under very dark skies, you can just about see it with your eyes alone. But binoculars or a good backyard telescope will make it much easier to find. Through a telescope, it looks like a tiny blue-green disc. Its colour comes from methane gas in its air, which takes in red sunlight.
why_it_matters: With binoculars or a telescope, you can spot a faraway planet yourself on a clear night.
